name: tui-firewall
tagline: The system firewall, with every change previewed before it runs
description:
A terminal UI for the Linux firewall. It shows the rules you actually have — action, direction, ports, source, destination, app profile, IPv6 and `route` rules included — alongside the default policies and the logging level.

The UI never builds a command line. It talks to a backend behind an interface, which returns a firewall-neutral model and produces command values; the confirm dialog shows that value and hands the same one to the runner, so what you read is what executes. `ufw` today, `firewalld` behind the same interface next.

Run `tui-firewall --demo` to drive an in-memory sample firewall: every key works, every command is built and previewed for real, and nothing touches your system.

pacman.note: Add the tui-tools repository to pacman.conf first.

aur.note: The -bin package installs the released static binary.

apt.note: Add the tui-tools apt repository and its keyring first.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-firewall/releases/download/v{version}/tui-firewall_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-firewall
sudo install -m0755 tui-firewall /usr/local/bin/tui-firewall
binary.note: One static binary. Verify it against checksums.txt from the same release.

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-firewall
cd tui-firewall && make build
sudo install -m0755 bin/tui-firewall /usr/local/bin/tui-firewall

security.needs_sudo: Reading ufw's state needs root, and so does every change: add, delete, enable, disable, reload, default policy and logging level. Escalation goes through `sudo -n`, which never prompts, and `--sudo ""` runs the command directly when you are already root.
